overview: Students looking to gain advanced technical knowledge and professional skills in structural engineering, construction technology, geotechnical engineering, transportation infrastructure, and sustainable building design should consider **studying Postgraduate (PG) Civil Engineering in France** as a wise choice. France boasts a strong higher education sector, advanced engineering research and an industry-oriented learning environment.

Students interested in applying for a **Master in Civil Engineering in France** can learn more about the specialized courses offered by French universities or engineering schools. They combine scientific knowledge, practical projects, research opportunities and technical training for graduates to pursue international engineering careers.

With ****Edu Hawk worldwide study abroad consultancy****, students can explore the best ****Civil Engineering courses in France**** to know the admission requirements and plan their journey to study abroad.

sections.title: 1. How long does a civil engineering postgraduate course in France last?

items: A **Master’s in Civil Engineering in France** lasts normally two years, divided in M1 and M2 for a total of 120 ECTS credits. Other engineering qualifications may be structured differently.

sections.title: 2. Yes, Indian students can do Postgraduate in Civil Engineering in France.

items: "Yes. **Indian students can pursue postgraduate course Civil Engineering in France** if they meet the academic, language and documentation requirements. Getting into a university and getting a student visa are two separate things.

sections.title: 3. Do I need to take the IELTS for civil engineering masters in France?

items: Not always. **Master's programs taught in English in France** can require IELTS, TOEFL, another recognized certificate or approved evidence of previous education in English. French-taught programs may have a specific level of French required, often at a specified CEFR level.

sections.title: 4. What are the tuition fees for Civil Engineering PG in France?

items: For 2026–2027, the reference fee for a national master’s degree at public institutions covered by this law is €255 per year for students from the EU/EEA/Switzerland and €3,950 for non-EU students subject to differentiated fees. Fees may be subject to exemptions and specific program arrangements.

sections.title: 5. What jobs can I get after completing a Civil Engineering PG in France?

items: Graduates may work in **structural engineering, geotechnical engineering, construction management, infrastructure development, BIM, transportation engineering, sustainable construction and research**. The opportunities depend upon the technical skills, experience, language proficiency and employer requirements.

sections.title: 6 . Which French universities have postgraduation programs in Civil Engineering?

items: **Université Paris-Saclay, Université Gustave Eiffel, INSA Lyon** are some of the schools to consider. Check the availability of the programs, specializations and entry requirements on their official university websites.

Students should have a clear idea of the qualification they will receive before enrolling in a ****postgraduate Civil Engineering program in France**.**

A French **national master's degree (diplôme national de master)** is a recognized degree in the French higher education system and the European higher education framework. It generally is equivalent to five years of study in higher education in conjunction with prior study at the bachelor level.
Before accepting an offer of admission, students should ensure that:
- Name and type of official qualification.
- The accreditation or authorization status of the institution.
- The length of the program and the academic credits.
- Requirements for recognition of your work or further studies in your country of choice.
- Any professional licensing requirements applicable to civil engineering work.
Indian students intending to return to India after their studies should check recognition requirements with prospective employers, universities and relevant authorities.

sections.title: 9. Civil Engineering PG Salary & Job Opportunities in France**

items: Graduates of a ****Master’s in Civil Engineering in France**** can take on technical, design, research and project-oriented roles. The job prospects depend on the selected specialization, internships, practical experience, language skills and hiring conditions.
Some of the popular ****career opportunities after Civil Engineering PG in France**** are:
- Civil Design Engineer
- Engineer, Structural
- Geotechnical Engineer
- Construction Project Engineer
- Construction or Site Engineer
- BIM Engineer or BIM Coordinator
- Engineer, Transportation Infrastructure
- Hydraulic Engineer
-  Material Testing Engineer
- Sustainability or Building Performance Engineer
- Research and Development Engineer

Graduates can find employment in **French construction companies, engineering consultancies, infrastructure contractors, transportation organizations, materials laboratories and public or private research organisations**.
Salary after PG in Civil Engineering in France

There is no one salary for all **Civil Engineering graduates in France. Salary packages vary by location, employer, job role, work experience, language skills and whether the position is an internship, graduate role or experienced appointment.

Students are expected to review current job advertisements and salary surveys relevant to their chosen specialization. They must also consider taxes, social contributions, accommodation costs and other cost of living when considering possible job opportunities.

sections.title: 10. Documents for PG in Civil Engineering in France**

items: Students applying for **postgraduate Civil Engineering courses in France** usually need to prepare the following documents:
- Passport ( valid ).
- Bachelor’s degree certificate or provisional degree certificate.
- Transcripts (official)
- CV or résumé.
- Motivation Letter (Statement of Purpose).
- Letters of recommendation, if applicable.
- Results of English-language tests, where applicable.
- If applicable, certification in the French language.
- Course descriptions or syllabus if required.
- Description of a relevant engineering project or internship.
- Certificates of employment or experience, if any.
- Passport size photographs, if needed.
- Proof of payment of the application fee (if applicable).
Some universities require that documents be translated into either French or English. French student visa applications may also require extra financial, accommodation and identity documents.
